title: Fractions
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 8; not yet checked by a Kenyan maths teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Official outcomes a and b are tested; c (use IT) and d (promote use) are not questions. Grade 7 taught each operation on its own; Grade 8 combines them, so the skills are the order of operations, brackets and 'of', mixed numbers in a combined question, and the three real-life shapes: the rest of a whole, a fraction of what is left, and buying or sharing by fractions. Teacher to confirm: whether 'of' is taught as a separate step in the order (BODMAS with O) in Kenyan classrooms.

skills.key_step: The child circles the division or multiplication and works it first, turning the divisor upside down, before any adding or subtracting.
representations: the question with the first step circled
steps: Work it first (÷ means multiply by the reciprocal).

board.do: Point at the ÷ sign.
board.say: Which part do we work first?

board.do: Wait for the child to choose.
The child circles 1/2 ÷ 2/3 and works it.

misconceptions.ask: Which comes first, divide or subtract?
What do we do to the second fraction when we divide?
Which fraction are we dividing by?
Are the pieces the same size?
Can top and bottom both be divided?

skills.key_step: The child works the bracket to a single fraction first and reads "of" as a multiplication done before adding.

board.do: Point at the bracket.
Wait for the child to say 5/6.
Write 5/6 × 3/5 underneath.

misconceptions.ask: What do brackets tell us?
What does 2/3 of 12 mean?
Is "of" a multiplication?
Did both fractions in the bracket get multiplied?
misconceptions.repair: Make the bracket one fraction first.

skills.key_step: The child rewrites every mixed number as an improper fraction before multiplying or dividing.

floor.prerequisite: Changes a mixed number to an improper fraction.
floor.question: 1 3/4 as an improper fraction

steps: Change mixed numbers to improper fractions.
Change back to a mixed number.

board.do: Draw one whole circle and a half circle for 1 1/2.
Point at the circles.
board.say: How many halves are there in all?

board.do: Wait for the child to say 3.

misconceptions.ask: Did the 1 get multiplied by the 1/3?
Where did the 1 go?
How many thirds in 2 wholes?
How many wholes in 5/4?

skills.key_step: The child adds the fractions used, takes the sum from one whole, and only then finds that fraction of the quantity in the unit asked.
steps: Change the whole to the unit asked.
contexts: a shamba with maize, beans and grass
a salary spent on rent and food

board.do: Draw a rectangle for the shamba split into 12 equal plots.
The child shades 1/3 for maize and 1/4 for beans.
Point at the unshaded plots.
Wait for the child to say.

misconceptions.ask: Is that the crops or the grass?
misconceptions.repair: The grass is what is left.

misconceptions.ask: What about the beans?
Are both fractions of the same shamba?
Minutes or hours?
How many acres is 5/12 of 12?

checks.question: A 20 acre farm: 2/5 tea, 1/4 maize, the rest bananas. Acres of bananas?
A 6 hour trip: 1/2 driving, 1/3 resting, the rest eating. Minutes eating?

skills.key_step: The child writes what is left after the first step and points to it as the new whole before taking the next fraction.

floor.prerequisite: Finds a fraction of a quantity.
floor.question: 3/4 of 6,000

representations: a tank drawn with water level
steps: Take the next fraction of that.
Answer what is asked: used or left.
contexts: pocket money spent in two shops

board.do: Draw a tank 3/4 full of water.
Point at the water.
Wait for the child to say.
Ask: the school uses 1/3 of this water. Of the water, or of the tank?

misconceptions.ask: Is that the water or the empty part?
A third of what?
misconceptions.repair: Of the water that is there.

misconceptions.ask: Is that used or left?
Is 1/3 of the water the same as 1/3 of the tank?

checks.question: A 90 kg sack: 1/3 sold, then 1/2 of the rest eaten. Kg left?
A 2,000 litre tank is 4/5 full; 1/4 of the water is used. Litres used?

skills.key_step: The child asks whether the story builds up a cost (multiply) or counts how many fit (divide) before calculating.

floor.prerequisite: Divides a whole number by a fraction.

steps: Whole pieces only: drop the part.

board.do: Draw a 6 m strip of cloth.
Point at the strip.
board.say: If each piece is 3/4 m, will there be more or fewer than 6 pieces?

board.do: Wait for the child to predict.
The child marks 3/4 m pieces along the strip.

misconceptions.ask: Should 3/4 kg cost more or less than 1 kg?
Will small pieces give more or fewer pieces?
Is the last piece a full piece?
Is that one fifth or two fifths?

checks.question: Sugar at 160 shillings a kg. Cost of 3/4 kg?
How many 1/4 kg packets from 5 kg of sugar?
